rationale: Crum: 'mire, mist, fog.' Second of the five elements of darkness in this enumeration; semantically close to 'smoke' in the standard Manichaean schema of five dark worlds.

Lyc. for ⲣⲱⲕϩ 'burn, blaze.' Fifth dark element; the verb is intransitive 'to burn' and the nominalized form names the element of fire as continuous activity rather than static substance — fits correspondential principle.
Coptic ⲥⲓϣⲉ 'bitter, bitterness'; the bitter element of the dark vehicle, paralleling 'bitter water' in Manichaean cosmology.
Lyc. ⲃⲁⲛⲓⲡⲉ = Sah. ⲃⲉⲛⲓⲡⲉ 'iron.' Used several times on this page for the metal that cannot pierce matter's body.
Lyc. ⲍⲁⲙⲧ̄ = Sah. ϩⲟⲙⲧ̄ 'bronze, copper.' Standard sequence with iron and lead.
Lyc. ⲧⲁⲍⲧ̄ = Sah. ⲧⲁϩⲧ̄ 'lead.' Completes the metals sequence iron/bronze/lead in line 14.
Greek loanword κοπίς 'cleaver, butcher's knife.' Used as the cutting-tool that has no power against the archonic body of matter.
Greek loanword πλάστης 'molder, fashioner.' The agent who shapes Matter — paired here with the verb ⲕⲱⲧ 'mold, fashion.' Distinct from ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ 'thing-molded' (already in vocabulary).
Greek loanword ζωγραφεῖν 'to paint, depict from life.' Lyc. ⲍ for ζ. Used reflexively: Matter 'painted herself' through the nature of the dark land — i.e. she gave herself her own image.
Greek loanword ὁμιλία with Lyc. ⲍ-onset. Standard 'speech, conversation, association.'
Greek loanword ἐπίκλησις. Technical term for ritual invocation/conjuring — fits the magical-speech register of this section.
Greek loanword ἐπικαλεῖν. Verbal pair with the noun ⲉⲡⲓⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲥ — Matter invokes her hidden son through speech-magic.
Lyc. ϩⲓⲕ 'magic.' Plural ⲛⲓⲍⲓⲕ 'the magics (of today)' — the contemporary magical arts identified as mysteries of the dark kingdom.

proposed_english: to live as a citizen / consort
rationale: Greek loanword πολιτεύεσθαι 'to live one's life, conduct oneself.' Translated 'lives' for the soul that lives among the dark members and walks in the members of Error.
Probably Lyc. ⲡⲱϣ 'measure, portion, share' — fits the simile 'like a measure of irons made red-hot from fire.' Confidence moderate.
